diagnostics: All infrastructure, district names, coordinates and numerical inputs are fictional synthetic data; source URLs are null.
Generator 1.0; data synthetic_corridor_v1; seed 42. Row provenance applies to every numerical field in that row.
Mass uses kg_LPG; supply, demand and capacities use kg_LPG/day. Daily periods are 1..H in Asia/Kolkata.
Daily demand is constant over the horizon: approximately 12% essential, 63% household and the remainder business, rounded to whole kg; these groups and shares are illustrative.
Source stocks begin at zero. District carry-in stocks are 1.5--2.4 days of demand; upstream buffers are explicit. There are no pre-horizon shipments.
Dispatch on day t arrives on t + lead_days. Zero-lead links permit same-day transfer only through an acyclic network; late arrivals remain in transit.
The domestic refinery branch is independent exogenous supply. An import shock does not reduce domestic production.
The alternate east-to-west depot route is capped at 5500 kg_LPG/day. The reserve storage-to-depot route is explicitly inactive.
Node dispatch is the total outbound mass per day; route capacity is a separate bound. There are no inferred storage ceilings, losses, costs or emissions factors.
SVG coordinates are diagram layout only, not geolocation. Route distances are synthetic logistics proxies, not verified transport distances.
Global assumption: demand_multiplier=1 applies to all district/group demand on every day.
Global assumption: extra_lead_days=0 applies to every originally active route for the entire horizon.
Exposure follows originally active downstream dependencies, including the selected disrupted route as a trigger; it does not prove actual shipments or shortages.
Policy illustrative_priority_v1 v1.0 is illustrative, not official authority.
Single-thread GLOP; fixed sorted variable order; exact sequential objective locks; independent absolute 1e-5 kg feasibility checks.
Unmet demand is lost service, not backlog. Post-horizon arrivals are in transit and cannot serve this horizon.
Fairness is aggregated across the horizon; earliest service is not an objective. Equally optimal daily schedules can differ across solver versions.
Binding labels identify tight primal bounds, not a causal sensitivity analysis or an IIS.

comparison.explanation: Both plans leave the same total unmet demand within 0.00001 kg. Inspect district/group distribution and logistics; no total-demand improvement is claimed.
comparison.baseline_method: Pooled supply/stock proportional targets by priority tier; minimise absolute deviations, then maximise remaining tier service, then logistics.
comparison.candidate_method: Maximise and lock each tier's service; minimise within-tier proportional deviations at achieved totals; minimise logistics last.
comparison.objective_scope: Fairness is district/group aggregate over the horizon. Earlier daily service is not an additional objective.
comparison.proxy_warning: Distance is synthetic shipment-mass × route-distance, not vehicle kilometres. No cost or emissions factors supplied.
